name: Michal
charge: Despising the king in her heart for dancing before the ark; how glorious was the king of Israel to day
summary: As the ark came into the city of David with shouting and the sound of the trumpet, Michal the daughter of Saul looked through a window, saw the king leaping and dancing before the Lord, and despised him in her heart. She had once been a tower against death to him, letting him down through a window out of her father’s reach; now she met him at the door with sarcasm. In the midst of pure righteousness she was out of the spirit, hating him instead of rejoicing. Michal had no child to the day of her death.
offenseFull: David danced before the Lord with all his might, girded with a linen ephod, and he and all the house of Israel brought up the ark with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet; and as the ark came into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked through a window, saw king David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and despised him in her heart (2 Samuel 6:14-16; 1 Chronicles 15:29). He was happy and he was in the spirit, because the Lord had chosen him to bring the ark back among the people, and he was clothed with a robe of fine linen along with the Levites and the singers (1 Chronicles 15:27). The people were dressed well and the day was holy. This is the same Michal who had loved him and saved his life when her father sent messengers to slay him in the morning, letting him down through a window and laying an image in the bed; a married woman is a tower against death to her husband, and that night she was one (1 Samuel 19:11-17). But here is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord’s day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High. David set the ark in the tabernacle he had pitched for it, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts, and dealt to every one, both men and women, a cake of bread, a good piece of flesh and a flagon of wine (2 Samuel 6:17-19). Then he returned to bless his own household, still in a good mood, and Michal came out to meet him and said sarcastically how glorious the king of Israel had been that day, uncovering himself in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself (2 Samuel 6:17-20; 2 Samuel 6:20). She had watched from a distance and could think of nothing but the king dancing with his clothes flying, on the day the ark of God came home to Israel. She forgot the greatness of the day and let a murmuring spirit take her.
judgmentFull: David answered that it was before the Lord, who chose him before her father and before all his house to appoint him ruler over the people of the Lord, therefore he would play before the Lord; and he would yet be more vile than this and base in his own sight, and of the maidservants she had spoken of he would be had in honour (2 Samuel 6:21-22; 2 Samuel 6:21-23). The office was a gift from the One before whom he was dancing, not a reason to hold himself too great to rejoice. Her real quarrel was older than the dance: the man leaping before the ark was the man who had replaced her father on the throne, and she was the daughter of Saul. Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death (2 Samuel 6:20-23; 2 Samuel 6:23). The Lord shut her womb. Do not play with the Most High. The earth is disquieted by an odious woman when she is married (Proverbs 30:23), and the adulterous woman of the proverb eats and wipes her mouth and says she has done no wickedness (Proverbs 30:20); the common thread is a woman who will not hold herself accountable. It is better to keep house where there is an evil wife than to bring her among the people (Ecclesiasticus 42:6). The king came home to bless his household, and the household met the blessing with reproach; the record closes her account not with her dignity preserved but with a childless house.

text.text: And David danced before the Lord with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
And as the ark of the Lord came into the city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the Lord; and she despised him in her heart.

And it came to pass, as the ark of the covenant of the Lord came to the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looking out at a window saw king David dancing and playing: and she despised him in her heart.

And David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, and all the Levites that bare the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the master of the song with the singers: David also had upon him an ephod of linen.

Saul also sent messengers unto David’s house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning: and Michal David’s wife told him, saying, If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain.
So Michal let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.
And Michal took an image, and laid it in the bed, and put a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster, and covered it with a cloth.
And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, He is sick.
And Saul sent the messengers again to see David, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.
And when the messengers were come in, behold, there was an image in the bed, with a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster.
And Saul said unto Michal, Why hast thou deceived me so, and sent away mine enemy, that he is escaped? And Michal answered Saul, He said unto me, Let me go; why should I kill thee?
And they brought in the ark of the Lord, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.
And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.

And he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.

And David said unto Michal, It was before the Lord, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the Lord, over Israel: therefore will I play before the Lord.
